draft.title: Composition and direction of trade
card: the mix of goods and services a country buys and sells, such as wine, machinery or tourism.
the countries a country trades with, such as which ones buy its exports and which ones supply its imports.
Composition answers the question: what is traded? Direction answers the question: who is it traded with?
A country can change one without changing the other. It may sell new products to the same partners, or sell the same products to new partners.
draft.remember: Composition is what a country trades. Direction is who it trades with.

a.q: Chile sells copper, fruit and wine to other countries. Which part of its trade does this list describe?
opts: The size of its trade debt
The number of its trading partners
a.why: The list shows what Chile sells, so it describes the composition of its trade. Direction would name the countries that buy these goods, which the list does not do.
a.clue: The list names goods, not countries.

b.q: Last year Kenya sold tea mostly to Pakistan. This year it sells the same tea, but mostly to Egypt. What has changed?
opts: The direction of trade, but not the composition
The composition of trade, but not the direction
Both the composition and direction of trade
Neither the composition nor the direction of trade
b.why: The goods stayed the same, so the composition did not change. The countries buying the tea changed, so the direction did. Composition is wrong because it is about the goods, not the buyers.
b.clue: Did the goods change, or the buyers?

b.best: The direction of trade, but not the composition
